preamble: Allophonic labialization of /h/ to the voiceless bilabial fricative [ɸ] before rounded vowels. In Standard Japanese /h/ is realized as [ɸ] before /u/, so ふ /hu/ is pronounced [ɸɯ]. Kyeongsang Korean shows a variable version of the same rule before back high vowels.

examples.note: /h/ is realized as [ɸ] before /u/, coarticulated with the lip compression of the vowel
Same allophone; the vowel is devoiced between voiceless consonants
Contrasts with [h] before /a, e, o/ and [ç] before /i/
Variable realization in about 10% of tokens in Shamrin's corpus; not categorical

context: Before the high back vowel /u/ (Japanese [ɯ]); variably before /u, ɯ/ in Kyeongsang Korean
sources: Okada, H. (1991). Japanese. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 21(2), 94–96. https://doi.org/10.1017/S002510030000445X
Itô, J., & Mester, A. (1995). Japanese phonology. In J. Goldsmith (Ed.), The Handbook of Phonological Theory (pp. 817–838). Blackwell.
Shamrin, A. S. (2022). The phoneme /h/ in Kyeongsang Korean. Siberian Journal of Philology 1, 210–220. https://doi.org/10.17223/18137083/78/15
